label: input token f at original position >= 3
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter f during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions t >= 3. Zero false positives on dev; misses are only tiny (~0.02) activations on other tokens at step 7. Magnitude grows with position: roughly 0.25-0.3 of max at t=3, ~0.6 at t=4, ~0.8 at t=5, near max by t=7, independent of whether f is a first or repeated occurrence. Does not fire on f at t=0-2, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase (including when f is fed back or output), and essentially never on other tokens.

issues: No systematic counterexamples found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.993, F1 0.996 and mass recall 0.9998. It has 0 false positives. The 422 misses hold 0.0% of the activation mass: scattered activations of about 0.01-0.02 at step 7-8 on various tokens (g, i, 2, t, c, e), with no single token driving them.
Checked and confirmed: f in the copy phase (predicate in_tok==f & phase!=0) never fires (0 of 90787 steps). By-t profile is 0 at t=0-2 and t>=9, and 0 on the delimiter and copy phase.

Checked and confirmed: magnitude does not depend on f having appeared earlier. Restricting to seen([f]) keeps precision 1.0 but recall drops to 0.146, about the base rate of an earlier f. Examples show a repeated f firing at the usual level for its position (e.g. t=3 f:0.29, t=7 f:0.99). The rise with position matches the examples (t=3 about 0.25-0.3, t=4 about 0.6, t=5 about 0.8, t=7 about 1.0).
Minor: there are no activations at t=9+ only because t=8 is the last original position (L<=9). This matches the label.
